findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact-match query (BlockedEmail.where(email: email)) against the raw email string passed in from the user record, and User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] without downcasing or stripping. The fabricator and any manually curated blocklist entries will be lowercase, so a signup with 'BAD@spammers.org' will not match a blocklist entry for 'bad@spammers.org', even though those are the same mailbox in practice. Anyone blocked can re-register (or re-attempt) by simply changing the case of their address, defeating the feature this PR adds. The email should be normalized (e.g., Email.downcase(email).strip) both when storing BlockedEmail rows and when looking them up.

findings.title: Validator performs a database write, and signups double-count match statistics
findings.body: EmailValidator.validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), which increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and saves the BlockedEmail record — i.e., running model validations now has a write side effect. This is fragile in itself (validations can run in contexts where writes are unexpected), and it produces incorrect statistics in the main signup flow: UsersController#create calls user.valid? (line 168, app/controllers/users_controller.rb) to decide whether to contact the Discourse hub, and then user.save runs validations again, so a single blocked signup attempt increments match_count twice. The stats update should be moved out of the validation path (e.g., done once in the controller) or de-duplicated.

findings.title: Moved whitelist/blacklist domain logic has no test coverage
findings.body: The PR moves the email_domains_whitelist / email_domains_blacklist restriction logic out of User#email_validator into the new EmailValidator class, and removes the old User model code. The new spec only exercises the BlockedEmail branch (stubbing BlockedEmail.should_block?); there are no tests asserting that a non-whitelisted domain is rejected, that a blacklisted domain is rejected, or that an allowed domain passes. If the moved logic broke (e.g., the elsif precedence between whitelist and blacklist, or regex construction in email_in_restriction_setting?), nothing in this PR's tests would catch it. Tests covering the whitelist and blacklist branches should be added (or the old user email-restriction specs kept/pointed at the new validator).
